consistency_gate.survivorship_note: SURVIVORSHIP-SELECTED SAMPLE. The wallets in this file are the ones that still hold the token, so the universe contains winners by construction. Wallets that bought and then sold out entirely are absent, and a wallet that was admitted to the scan and later decayed may be missing from the screened universe. A verdict produced on this sample cannot be read as 'the gate found no good traders' - it can only be read as 'these particular wallets failed the gate'.
consistency_gate.price_cap_note: HISTORY MAY BE TRUNCATED. Prices are read per trade, and the per-wallet block cap limits how many distinct blocks a single wallet scan prices. Where the cap bites, the most RECENT blocks are priced and the number of blocks skipped is reported rather than hidden, so a wallet's early history can be missing from the PnL.
consistency_gate.upstream_provenance: the artefacts in this package are fetched live and cached to disk; the sections below report what those files contain

The value 637 is this spec's arithmetic from that formula at p0=0.50, p1=0.55, alpha=0.05 one-sided, beta=0.20, delta=0.05 (the parameters are ANALYST_CHOICE; the formula is CITED).

rows.label: Consistency ratio (positive periods / total periods)
rows.threshold_source: DEFINITION CITED: 'Consistency Ratio - A measure of how consistently the manager is able to exhibit positive excess returns. To calculate the consistency ratio, the number of months the manager had positive excess returns is divided by the total number of months.' NO MINIMUM IS PUBLISHED BY ANY AUTHORITY - the source says only 'The higher the number, the better.' The threshold field is null and the code must supply it from config, labelled ANALYST_CHOICE.
rows.authority: Principal Financial Group / Marietta Board of Pensions (institutional pension plan reporting convention)

rows.label: Minimum number of periods required for a consistency ratio to be reported
rows.threshold_source: The 36-observation floor is CITED (GIPS 4.C.36, '36 monthly returns are not available'); the day/month period choice is ANALYST_CHOICE. On-chain analogue (36 daily observations) is an ANALYST ADAPTATION of a GIPS disclosure rule for composites.
rows.authority: CFA Institute (GIPS)

rows.label: Sortino ratio (excess return over downside risk)
rows.threshold_source: DEFINITION CITED (CFA Institute, 'The Sortino Ratio'): 'S = (Mean portfolio return - MAR) / Downside deviation' and 'it is calculated in the same way as the Sharpe ratio except that the MAR replaces the risk-free rate in the numerator and downside deviation replaces standard deviation in the denominator'. NO BAND IS PUBLISHED - CFA Institute publishes no interpretation threshold. The threshold field is null; any threshold used is ANALYST_CHOICE.
rows.authority: CFA Institute (Deborah Kidd, CFA, Investment Performance Measurement, H17004, 2012)
rows.gap: computed or reported in code, but NOT enforced: no gate in the four enforcement modules can reject a wallet on this criterion
rows.note: computed and reported; CFA Institute publishes the definition and no band, so there is nothing to gate on

rows.label: Calmar ratio (return per unit of maximum drawdown)
rows.threshold_source: FORMULA CITED (peer-reviewed): 'CR(R_p,T) = E(R_p - R_f)/MAXDD(T)' (Wang, Kresta & Tichy, Computational Management Science 21, art. 17, 2024). NO BAND IS PUBLISHED. NOTE: the original 36-month window from Terry W. Young (1991) could NOT be verified against the primary source - it is recorded in AUTHORITATIVE_CONSISTENCY_STANDARDS.md section 5.2 as UNVERIFIED against the primary, and is therefore NOT used as a threshold here.
rows.authority: Anlan Wang, Ales Kresta, Tomas Tichy - Computational Management Science (Springer), open access
rows.gap: computed or reported in code, but NOT enforced: no gate in the four enforcement modules can reject a wallet on this criterion
rows.note: computed and reported; no published band exists

rows.label: Maximum drawdown ceiling
rows.threshold_source: NO NUMERICAL THRESHOLD IS PUBLISHED BY CFA INSTITUTE. The source lists maximum drawdown as an APPRAISAL RATIO that 'measure investment skill' and that 'must be used with care, noting the assumptions of each ratio'. The threshold field is null and any ceiling is ANALYST_CHOICE.

rows.label: Minimum track-record length before a performance claim is publishable
rows.threshold_source: CITED: GIPS 1.A.3 (five years to claim compliance), 4.A.1(a) and 6.A.1(a) (build up to 10 years), 8.C.1(a) (one-, three-, five-year presentations); SEC 17 CFR 275.206(4)-1(d)(2) (one-, five-, ten-year periods, 'if the relevant portfolio did not exist for a particular prescribed period, then the life of the portfolio must be substituted for that period'). 1825 days = 5 years, the SEC/GIPS figure expressed in days for code.

rows.label: Minimum distinct tokens traded (independence of the bet set)
rows.threshold_source: NO AUTHORITY LOCATED PUBLISHES A DISTINCT-TOKEN MINIMUM for a trader. ANALYST_CHOICE. Related CITED concept: Grinold's breadth counts only INDEPENDENT bets, and the GMGN vendor convention scores token_num (diversity) at 10% of its published composite score - see crypto_vendor_composite_weights.

rows.label: Edge decay: recent performance materially worse than early performance
rows.threshold_source: NO AUTHORITY LOCATED PUBLISHES A DECAY THRESHOLD. ANALYST_CHOICE, threshold field null. Supporting CITED concept: Bailey & Lopez de Prado's performance-degradation statistic in 'The Probability of Backtest Overfitting' Section 3.2 measures the decline from IS to OOS performance of the selected strategy, and CFA Institute notes appraisal ratios 'help identify manager skill (as opposed to luck)'.

rows.label: Bayesian split-half posterior stability (does the skill claim survive removing the early history?)
rows.threshold_source: MODEL CITED: Bayes Rules! Ch.3 Eq. (3.10) posterior; Ch.4 'Sequential analysis: Evolving with data' and 'Proving data order invariance' establish that the posterior is order-invariant, which is what makes a time-split holdout legitimate. The comparison rule and any stability band are ANALYST_CHOICE - no source publishes a split-half posterior stability bar for traders.
rows.authority: Barber, Bay & Solberg, 'Bayes Rules!' (CRC Press), Chapters 3-4
rows.gap: computed or reported in code, but NOT enforced: no gate in the four enforcement modules can reject a wallet on this criterion

rows.threshold_source: CITED: CFA Institute GIPS 3.A.9 'Terminated portfolios must be included in the historical performance of the composite up to the last full measurement period that each portfolio was under management and for which the firm has discretion'; 3.A.6 'Any change to a composite definition must not be applied retroactively'; 3.A.7 timely and consistent inclusion.
rows.authority: CFA Institute (GIPS for Firms, 2020)

price_method.method: Uniswap V2 pair reserves read at each trade's own block, via a keyless archive RPC. The package asks the V2 factory, AT that block, which pair existed for (token, USDC), then reads that pair's getReserves() at the same block and takes reserve(quote) / reserve(token) with decimals applied. A token whose deep pair is quoted in WETH is priced in WETH and multiplied by the WETH/USD price read from the deep WETH/USDC pair at the same block. No price API is required for the pool route.

liquidity_floor.note: a pair whose quote side holds less than the floor is REJECTED and the price is reported as unavailable rather than as a number, so a nearly-empty pool cannot manufacture a price

per_wallet_block_cap.consequence: the cap limits how many DISTINCT blocks one wallet scan prices. When it bites, the most RECENT blocks are priced - those are the trades that decide whether the wallet has a live edge - and the number of blocks NOT priced is reported rather than hidden. A wallet's EARLY history can therefore be missing from its realised PnL, and its PnL can be incomplete without the PnL itself being wrong.

social_edge.measured_lead_times_note: NO WALLET HAS YET BEEN MEASURED AGAINST A REAL MEMBER-COUNT SERIES. No artefact on disk records a lead time between a wallet's buy and a community-size event.
social_edge.why_not_measurable: A member-count series only becomes a SERIES over time: the endpoints expose the CURRENT count, so the series has to be sampled repeatedly, and a lead time needs at least two observations that bracket the wallet's purchase. The stored series cover minutes, not days, and their member counts do not move, so no threshold crossing can be located inside them. Until the series has been collected over a real interval, the honest answer is NOT YET MEASURABLE - not 'no effect' and not a lead time computed from a flat line.
social_edge.narrative_classifier_note: the specificity score is a weighted classifier over free signals that separate a community footprint from a trend clone. Its weights and keyword list are analyst choices and are re-scorable; it measures the PRESENCE of a community footprint, not attention, sentiment or community size.

keyed_source.free_tier_note: these actions were verified live against Etherscan V2 on the date recorded in the adapter's own source comment; anything not listed as working returns HTTP 200 with status=0 and message=NOTOK.
keyed_source.http_error_convention: Etherscan signals failure in the JSON BODY, not the HTTP status. A bad key, a bad parameter and a rate limit all return HTTP 200 with {"status":"0","message":"NOTOK"}. Every response must therefore be checked for status == "1"; an HTTP 200 is never proof of data.
keyed_source.url_separator_rule: the DefiLlama historical-price endpoint separates chain from token with a COLON: https://coins.llama.fi/prices/historical/{unix_ts}/{chain}:{token}. The comma form returns {"coins": {}} and looks like a dead endpoint - it is not.
keyed_source.url_separator_rule_source_line: Note the COLON between chain and token. The comma form returns
keyed_source.api_key_source: the process environment (ETHERSCAN_API_KEY), optionally loaded from the gitignored .secrets.env beside the package
keyed_source.api_key_presence_note: presence was read through the package's own accessor, which returns a boolean
keyed_source.api_key_handling: the key is read from the environment at call time. It is never a literal in source, never written into any artefact, report, chart or log, and no fingerprint or hash of it is produced. This section reports only WHETHER one is configured, never its value.
keyed_source.holder_list_workaround: Etherscan's own tokenholderlist action is Pro-only and returns NOTOK on the free tier, so it is not used. Holder balances are read with the free-tier balance actions, or reconstructed by netting the token's transfer tape.

IMPORTANT HOST FACT: api.coingecko.com is UNREACHABLE from this host. Four separate live probes all failed with ConnectionResetError (WinError 10054) during the TLS handshake, and the raw TLS handshake to the resolved Cloudflare IPs (104.20.41.132, 172.66.172.219) fails the same way. Plain HTTP does not help - it 302s to the local URL filter at 192.168.8.1/urlfilter and returns a 'Sangfor NGAF' block page WITH HTTP 200 (a false positive). pro-api.coingecko.com answers normally (HTTP 401 'API Key Missing') and www.coingecko.com answers (HTTP 404 on API paths), so the block is hostname-specific. Do not treat any 200 from this host as CoinGecko data.

source_reliability.interpretation_rule: a status code alone is not proof of data on this host. A blocked host can answer HTTP 200 with an HTML block page, a JSON endpoint can answer HTTP 200 with an API-level error, and a docs page can answer HTTP 200 at a path that is supposed to return JSON. Every count below is therefore reported with the shape of the response, not just its status.

gaps.gap: The wallets scored are the ones that still hold the token. Wallets that bought and sold out entirely are absent, so the sample cannot show what fraction of the universe is skilled.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a scan over a published, non-survivorship-selected wallet universe with the admission rule recorded

gaps.gap: The per-wallet block cap means a wallet's early history may not be priced at all, so its realised PnL can be incomplete. The blocks skipped are reported, but the un-priced history is gone.
gaps.what_would_close_it: an uncapped per-wallet price pass, or a per-wallet record of which blocks were skipped and why

gaps.gap: Realised PnL is GROSS of gas, DEX fees and MEV. None of those are observable from ERC-20 transfers alone, so every PnL figure overstates what a wallet kept.
gaps.what_would_close_it: per-swap gas and fee logs, joined to the transfer tape

gaps.gap: These criteria in the specification have no implementation token in the four enforcement modules: crypto_vendor_composite_weights.
gaps.what_would_close_it: an implementation in edge.py, pbo.py, traders.py or priced.py

gaps.gap: These criteria are computed or reported but CANNOT reject a wallet, so their presence in the code is not evidence that the standard is applied: min_independent_bets_table, wilson_lower_bound_above_chance, bonferroni_alpha_per_test, bh_fdr_procedure, multiple_testing_t_statistic_hurdle, sortino_ratio, calmar_ratio, max_drawdown, drawdown_duration, track_record_length_minimum, chain_coverage_ceiling, posterior_split_half_stability, cross_chain_comparability_report, crypto_vendor_win_rate_band, crypto_vendor_pnl_ratio, vendor_label_not_a_standard.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a gate that compares the quantity against the threshold

gaps.gap: 3 of the 31 criteria have NO published standard behind them. Their thresholds are this package's operating choices.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a published source, or the explicit acceptance that the number is an analyst choice

gaps.gap: For these criteria the gate compares against a different number from the one the specification publishes: min_independent_bets. The published threshold is in the table; the value the code actually applies is named beside it.
gaps.what_would_close_it: aligning the gate's threshold with the published one, or recording the substitution as an analyst choice

gaps.gap: No wallet holds WHITELISTED status. The forward cohort is empty, so this package has not identified a consistently profitable memecoin trader.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a wallet that passes every hard gate with a non-trivial sample

gaps.gap: The state whitelist registry and the whitelist embedded in the priced-edge result file hold different sets of wallets, so one of them is stale. The report cannot say which without knowing which run produced each.
gaps.what_would_close_it: re-running the gate so both copies are written by the same run, or recording the run identifier in each

gaps.gap: The measured error against the reference index ranges from a few percent to roughly a quarter on a young, shallow pool. The price is the price of the pool the wallet traded, which is not always the price of the token.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a depth-weighted reference price, or the liquidity depth at each trade's block reported beside the price

gaps.gap: The scan covers ONE token over ONE window of 1000 blocks, with 2 buyer(s) inside it. That is a case study, not a rate.
gaps.what_would_close_it: the same scan run over a large, published set of launches

gaps.gap: Only buyers INSIDE the window are listed. A wallet that bought after the window is not an early buyer and is not in this file, so the file cannot be read as the set of buyers of the token.
gaps.what_would_close_it: the full buyer set with entry lags, or an explicit statement of the screened universe

gaps.gap: No wallet has been measured against a real member-count series, so no lead time is reported. The series must be collected over time before a lead time can mean anything.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a member-count series spanning days around a wallet's purchase

gaps.gap: The narrative specificity score is a weighted classifier over free signals whose weights and keyword list are analyst choices. It measures the presence of a community footprint; it does not measure attention, sentiment or size, and it is not a forward test of the paper's outperformance claim.
gaps.what_would_close_it: two cohort snapshots separated in time and a forward-return test on them

gaps.gap: The Etherscan holder-list and token-info actions are Pro-only, so on the free tier the holder set is reconstructed from the transfer tape rather than read from the vendor.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a Pro subscription, or a full transfer tape for the token

gaps.gap: On this host a blocked host can answer HTTP 200 with an HTML block page, and a JSON endpoint can answer HTTP 200 with an API-level error. Counts of 'working' sources are therefore counts of well-shaped responses, not of reachable data.
gaps.what_would_close_it: response-shape validation on every probe, which the catalogue partly does but not for every host

gaps.note: This section exists so the report cannot be read as claiming more than it delivers. Every entry says what is missing and what would close it.
